data.title: CLARITY Act back in the spotlight after $6.3B Binance hack — Here’s why!
data.description:
The $6.3 billion Binance hack, the largest crypto security incident on record, has sparked fresh debate over cryptocurrency regulations in the United States, particularly the need for stronger safeguards for crypto exchanges.

According to Senator Cynthia Lummis, the incident highlights why the proposed CLARITY Act is important for the industry’s future.

Lummis blames the CLARITY Act setback

The Senator argued that the legislation would have provided crypto firms with legal clarity to freeze suspicious transactions as soon as law enforcement agencies flagged them. This would have allowed exchanges to respond immediately to potential security threats, rather than lose valuable time navigating regulatory uncertainty.

Lummis added, 

Every minute lost is money gone for good.

Lummis also warned that hackers stole more than $6 billion in less than four hours, making the incident larger than the previous two biggest crypto thefts combined — the $3.5 billion LuBian hack in December 2020 and the $1.4 billion Bybit exploit in February 2025.

CFTC Chairman stresses on new crypto regulations

At the same time, CFTC Chair Mike Selig also used the incident to reinforce the need for a federal registration framework for crypto exchanges. He argued that offshore exchanges lack the cybersecurity safeguards expected of regulated U.S financial markets.

However, his remarks were focused on vulnerabilities in supporting infrastructure, such as an individual’s laptop, rather than weaknesses in blockchain networks or smart contracts. 

Additionally, he also highlighted how blockchain transparency could help regulators trace stolen funds, even when hackers use privacy tools such as Tornado Cash. 

Selig went on to say, 

I think the fact that we can trace transactions on-chain, even when some of these technologies are used to obfuscate that, gives us a lot of potential as a regulator to be really a cop on the beat.

This is evidence that the Binance hack is particularly alarming. Especially since the amount affected already exceeds the combined value of the next nine largest crypto hacks, according to Glassnode. 

Crypto market faces the brunt

Here, it’s worth pointing out that the impact has also extended beyond just security concerns, weighing on market sentiment and liquidity.

According to DefiLlama, DeFi Total Value Locked (TVL) dropped by 5.3% on 30th October to $83.95 billion, its lowest level since 21st August. Stablecoin supply also declined to $296.6 billion, remaining below the $300 billion-mark since 24th October.

Meanwhile, around $1.5 billion in leveraged positions were liquidated as Bitcoin [BTC] briefly fell to $76,400, triggering widespread selling across major cryptocurrencies.

While Pepe [PEPE], Sky [SKY], and Bitcoin Cash [BCH] posted gains, riskier assets such as MemeCore [M], Ethena [ENA], and Pump.fun [PUMP] recorded significant losses.

Therefore, going forward, $76,400 remains a crucial support level for Bitcoin, while reclaiming $80,000 could signal improving market sentiment. On the other hand, a break below $76,000 could extend the broader risk-off trend.

However, with Binance expecting to resume withdrawals within 48 hours (from the day the hack was reported), hope remains.

Final Summary

  • Senator Lummis is the latest to comment on the Binance hack and what could have been done to prevent it. 
  • DeFi TVL dropped by 5.3% to $83.95 billion, while stablecoin supply also fell to $296.6 billion.

data.title: How can PEPE traders take advantage of conflicting momentum signals?
data.description:
At the time of writing, PEPE was down 2.50% in the last 24 hours, its performance noticeably worse than other leading memecoins. For its part, Dogecoin [DOGE] was down by only 0.94%, while Shiba Inu [SHIB] gained by 1.13%.

And yet, the memecoin has rallied by 7.42% over the past week. In fact, Glassnode data also showed that the memecoin sector, as a whole, has shed 3.1% of its value over the past week, less than BTC’s 4.4% or ETH’s 5.9%.

Does PEPE have a longer-term bullish bias, and should swing traders and investors be looking to buy? Here’s what you need to know!

PEPE bulls battle for control of Value Area High

The 1-day chart revealed a bullish swing structure in place. The key levels to watch were $0.0000032 and $0.00000536. A daily session close above $0.00000536 would confirm a bullish trend continuation.

Within this swing move, the Fixed Range Volume Profile tool was used.

It plotted the Value Area Low and High at $0.00000377 and $0.00000491, meaning 70% of the trading volume since 11th September, when the impulse move began, has taken place within these two levels. This also makes them important horizontal levels to watch.

The A/D indicator fell to new lows following the heavy selling on 29th October. Meanwhile, the Awesome Oscillator stayed above the zero line.

These conflicting signals did not seem to subtract from the overall bullish price bias PEPE showed on the daily timeframe. However, ideally, buyers would want to see sustained demand to keep the uptrend going.

PEPE swing traders can maintain a bullish bias

Over the past week, PEPE has oscillated between $0.0000042 and $0.0000056, and at the time of writing, was at the mid-range level. The technical indicators were neutral, with a slight bearish leaning from the Awesome Oscillator.

Traders and long-term investors can stay bullish given the daily timeframe structure, but should be prepared for a price dip toward $0.0000044 or even $0.0000038. Especially if Bitcoin faces intense selling pressure.

Final Summary

  • PEPE has shed more value in the past 24 hours than some of the larger crypto memecoins.
  • Swing traders and investors can maintain a bullish bias as the price challenges the VAH once again.

data.title: BEAM’s price defies market trends with multi-month uptrend, but what should traders do?
data.description:
Gaming sector and ecosystem token Beam [BEAM] has rallied by 45.2% in the last 24 hours, with a 1,115% hike in daily trading volume. The $241.6 million market cap asset has been trending higher since July.

While the rest of the crypto sphere panicked and sold after news of the Binance heist broke, BEAM’s price surged across the board.

This relative strength was likely due to its existing bullish momentum. It was reported that the Beam Foundation had burned all the BEAM tokens in the possession of the Binance hacker.

984.249 million tokens worth around $3.37 million were burned using the Gnosis Safe Burn Signature, which also helped explain the short-term bullish outlook.

BEAM continues its multi-month uptrend

In June, BEAM broke above the downtrend’s lower high at $0.0016, flipping its structure bullishly. The latest bullish continuation came when the $0.00356-high, made on 23rd October, was breached on the 30th.

The breakout was on extraordinary volume and the gains continued at the time of writing. Relative to the rest of the market, the latest bullish impulse move was highly noticeable.

It is likely the altcoin may be overextended. The RSI on the daily chart was at 82, once again in overbought territory. This does not mean a pullback will immediately follow though. A stretch of ovebought RSI readings earlier in October came alongside a 16.54% move higher over ten days.

Traders’ call to action – Take profits and wait for a pullback

The 4-hour chart showed that there were two support zones of interest right now. The first was at $0.00445, which was respected over the past 24 hours as a demand zone and the altcoin went to challenge the $0.0054 local highs.

The other support zone to watch was the $0.0034 order block that initiated this move higher.

Swing traders can think about taking profits and waiting for a pullback, or moving their trailing stop loss order to just below $0.0034, as per their preferred strategy.

A pullback towards $0.0040 would likely provide a buying opportunity. However, without a clear sign of a short-term pullback, BEAM swing traders need to wait and not rush to look for a re-entry.

Final Summary

  • BEAM token has been on an uptrend on the daily timeframe since June.
  • Latest impulse move higher has not settled into a pullback yet, and swing traders can choose to wait for a revisit of key demand zones before buying.

data.title: RUNE up 15% after hackers use THORChain to launder stolen funds — What next?
data.description:
THORChain’s native token RUNE rallied by over 15% in the last 24 hours as the broader market lost $160 billion in capitalization. The decline followed Binance’s hack, which saw the centralized exchange (CEX) lose around $6.30 billion.

Hence, the question: Why is the token’s performance independent of the general market right now?

Is THORChain abetting laundering of funds from crypto hacks?

Hackers have regularly used THORChain to launder funds stolen from the crypto market.

For instance, funds from the Binance hack were commingled to a similar address that received $388 million from the Bitget incident after arriving via THORChain. This evidence might be a suggestion that the same actor is likely responsible.

The pattern has been evident from the swap volumes and fees on the chain, which have increased significantly. Fees hit a weekly high of $11K, confirming a spike in network activity.

Swap volumes showed that a total of $62.08 million went through the mainnet, while $94 million was processed through its bridges in other wallets.

As far as the hack is concerned, $8.94 million was converted to Bitcoin [BTC], and Ethereum [ETH] accounted for $6.17 million, while other tokens were swapped for $1.18 million.

As a result of a spike in network activity, the daily trading volume of RUNE surged by over 393%.

However, users are still worried that the chain could be abetting the laundering of funds. This, because other chains like Arbitrum One [ARB] froze the funds, but THORChain did not. In fact, immediately after the incident, THORChain posted,

Digital money needs digital freedom.

While they did not support the hack directly, the language used combined with the timing of the post raised many concerns. One user on X mocked the post, commenting,

Free to hack.

RUNE faces resistance at $0.70 despite strong buying

On the price charts, RUNE rose aggressively from $0.58 to $0.723, but it could not stay above $0.70 for long. The brief dip below $0.60 came immediately after the hack incident, but the altcoin reclaimed it as the floor.

The $0.70-level has been a resistance for the past month, but the strong buying pressure failed at this zone.

Moreover, the MACD bars turned green and grew bigger, asserting the buying pressure. The Chaikin Money Flow (CMF) reinforced capital inflows into the chain, rising from -0.04 to 0.31.

Therefore, RUNE will remain in a bearish structure on the 4-hour chart unless $0.70 is turned into support. Otherwise, the altcoin could continue bouncing between $0.60 and $0.70, but there is a chance it could break down.

Final Summary

  • RUNE surged by over 15% as hackers moved stolen funds via THORChain, leading to high network activity. 
  • RUNE bulls are facing resistance at $0.70 despite strong buying pressure, suggesting that the rally could be short-lived.

data.title: PYTH crypto sees $179M drop in secured value – Can prices recover?
data.description:
Pyth Network [PYTH] has recorded a massive decline over the past day, with the asset plummeting roughly 12% to a new local low at press time.

The reaction, expectedly, followed the Binance hack incident, which reportedly resulted in losses of roughly $6.3 billion. However, a closer look shows that the protocol has also recorded one of its weakest-performing months.

Perpetual market activity has further fueled the decline, as traders concentrate capital on shorting PYTH.

PYTH records a $179M capital outflow

The decline in PYTH was accompanied by a massive on-chain capital outflow, tracked through Total Value Secured (TVS).

TVS tracks the total value of assets managed by the protocol, including bridged and native tokens. The decline suggests that market participants are pulling back from active utility. Over the past day, TVS dropped from $3.164 billion to $2.985 billion, marking an outflow of $179 million in the past 24 hours as of writing .

More concerning is that Pyth Network’s earnings have also plummeted significantly over the past day, according to data from DeFiLlama. Earnings, which track gross profit after incentives, have fallen to roughly $1,310 at press time, the lowest level ever recorded on a monthly basis.

In fact, this represents a significant decline from September, when the protocol earned $434,640. When earnings drop to this level, it points to reduced protocol utility as users become more reluctant to engage with the platform.

Perpetual traders increase short positions

Sellers have dominated perpetual trading activity as they continue to expand their positions.

Funding Rate data for PYTH‘s perpetual market shows a significant concentration of short positions, with the rate falling to -0.0172 as of writing.

PYTH’s negative Funding Rate, now at an extreme level, shows that traders have positioned roughly $36.77 million in the perpetual market towards shorting the asset.

When broken down by trader category, the data shows that whales, traders who control large amounts of capital in the market, have been key participants influencing price dynamics.

The Whale-Retail Delta, which tracks the difference between whale and retail trading activity, rose to 0.301 over the past day as whale positioning in the asset continued to increase.

Spot traders accumulate despite the decline

Spot traders, despite the negative outlook, have been accumulating the asset.

According to CoinGlass, Spot Netflow tracks the inflow and outflow of capital on exchanges. When outflows exceed inflows, it suggests that more assets are being withdrawn from exchanges, potentially indicating accumulation.

Netflow currently stands at -$1.56 million, suggesting that following the decline, more capital has moved out of exchanges than into them. This outlook may stem from investors viewing the recent drop as a discount.

data.title: Wall Street’s Black Friday — Is a 2022-style crypto winter brewing?
data.description:
November is kicking off with unprecedented levels of market volatility.

The past 24 hours have been one big bloodbath. Tech stocks have been hit particularly hard. Over the last 24 hours, markets in the U.S, Japan, South Korea, China and Taiwan have combined to wipe $1.7 trillion off their market cap. This, after a flurry of earnings reports kicked off the “AI bubble” narrative again. 

The key takeaway? The market got a reality check. For instance, Alphabet lost more than 12% of its market value, highlighting just how quickly sentiment can turn when AI expectations collide with earnings reality.

However, it is the timing of this sell-off that is adding another layer of pressure to the crypto market.

According to the Kobeissi Letter, the probability of a Democratic sweep in next week’s U.S mid-term elections has risen by 7% to a record high of 72% over the last 2 days. This, as markets continue to accelerate their decline, adding another layer of macroeconomic uncertainty for the crypto market.

This leaves us with high rates, a falling stock market, $100+ oil prices, and rising CPI, PPI, and PCE inflation. Next week is going to be interesting, to say the least. 

However, the market isn’t entirely bearish just yet. 

Crypto’s 2022 playbook returns as market volatility builds

It’s been over a year since the October 2025 crash knocked down risk assets.

Bitcoin is still down over 30% from its pre-crash high of $126K. Considering the FUD surrounding U.S mid-terms, the Binance hack and recent tech sell-off, it seems the market still has a long way to go before any real recovery. This puts the question of whether crypto has found its bottom back in focus. 

Notably, the 2022 cycle could offer some clues. Back then, the FTX collapse was just about a year after BTC’s November 2021 high, lining up with the cycle bottom in late Q4 2022, when BTC dropped to $16K. What followed was a 155% rally, followed by another 120% run, pushing Bitcoin close to $108K by 2024.

So, could the ongoing volatility be setting crypto up for a 2022-style cycle?

Based on historical trends, Bitcoin falling below $80K and the overall market sell-off could allude to later phases of a crypto bottom. With macro uncertainty continuing to build, the market could be heading into the final stage of capitulation before a bounce back.

Thus, the risk-off trend will likely continue through year-end before the crypto sees a 2023-style uptrend.

Final Summary

data.title: Bitwise, Galaxy, and Morpho back CCI’s new framework for U.S crypto vault regulations
data.description:
The Crypto Council for Innovation (CCI) has proposed a new framework to bring crypto vaults under U.S securities laws.

In a 238-page report that was published on 29th October, the CCI outlined how regulators can assess different vault structures under existing securities regulations. This includes the Securities Act of 1933, the Investment Company Act of 1940, and the Investment Advisers Act of 1940.

90-year-old securities rules tested

For those unaware, crypto vaults are smart contracts that accept users’ token deposits and deploy them into financial strategies such as lending, borrowing, and investments to generate returns.

And, now their adoption is expanding beyond decentralized finance (DeFi), with traditional financial institutions also exploring their potential. In fact, according to S&P Global, assets deposited in vaults touched $131 billion in April 2026.

Hence, the CCI, along with members from Bitwise, Galaxy Digital, and Morpho, is arguing that crypto vaults should not automatically fall outside U.S federal securities laws just because they operate via blockchain technology and smart contracts.

Lending more weight to the proposal, Bitwise CEO Hunter Horsley said,

Vaults are going to change capital markets. We’re delighted to get to be a part of it.

CCI’s dual framework for crypto vaults

In its detailed report, CCI came up with a two-sided ‘Control Framework’ to resolve how much authority human operators hold over deposited assets. Additionally, the framework would also sort out how much control investors have over their funds.

Additionally, the report examined four factors on the operator’s side, which included mandate, execution, governance, and disposition. Here, the report assessed whether operators can select investment strategies, reallocate capital, change protocol rules, or move deposited assets.

Meanwhile, for the depositor’s side, there were six conditions considered. These included, comprehensibility, verifiability, observability, predictability, notice, and actionability.

So, the crux here is simple, and that is CCI wants vaults with immutable smart contracts, transparent operations, limited human discretion, and permissionless withdrawals to face a different regulatory assessment from those where operators retain significant control over investment decisions.

CCI’s way of bringing regulatory clarity to crypto markets

Interestingly, the proposal also draws parallels with Section 10301 of the proposed CLARITY Act. For those unaware, the latter addressed non-decentralized finance protocols based on whether identifiable individuals or groups could control or materially alter their functionality.

And, therefore, the CCI wants regulators to adopt a similarly control-based approach. In fact, for regulatory clarity, CCI also wants the SEC to follow the approach it previously adopted for ETFs. This would involve granting individual exemptions to qualifying vault structures under Section 6(c) of the Investment Company Act before gradually introducing broader, standardized rules.

Commenting on the same, Horsley added,

We worked with regulators for years to help make crypto ETFs possible. We’re happy to collaborate again, this time on vaults.

The red flag in question

Needless to say, the proposal also echoes SEC Commissioner Hester Peirce’s 22nd July statement, Headstands and Summervaults, in which she cautioned, against treating all crypto vaults alike.

Vaults are not uniform

Here, it’s worth pointing out a recent report by AMBCrypto which highlighted how Web3 protocols are increasingly moving away from their original promises of openness, permissionlessness, and decentralization.

The report stressed on projects such as Hyperliquid, Aave, and Polygon that have adopted models that prioritize internal vaults, buybacks, and treasury accumulation over directly distributing value to token holders.

Final Summary

  • The CCI is arguing that crypto vaults should not automatically fall outside U.S federal securities laws.
  • According to S&P Global, assets deposited in vaults hit $131 billion in April 2026.

data.title: Why AAVE crypto traders must watch $113 support after Binance hack
data.description:
Around 9 pm UTC on the 29th of October, a Binance hot wallet on Ethereum sent 63 ERC-20 tokens and 167,464 ETH in a single transaction. The same exploiter address received another 28,006 ETH in a second transaction from a second Binance hot wallet on Ethereum, along with funds from Arbitrum [ARB], Optimism [OP], and Avalanche [AAVE].

In response, the Aave markets across all networks were frozen, stopping everyone, including the exploiter, from opening new supply or borrow positions.

The broader market has reacted bearishly, with Bitcoin [BTC] and Ethereum [ETH] down 3.46% and 3.93% in the past 24 hours, compared to Aave’s 5.67%. The crypto market witnessed over $1.50 billion in liquidations, with a majority being long liquidations.

Is the long-term AAVE trend bullish?

From June to September, the DeFi token rallied by 214.2%, from $60 to $188. Since making this local high, the altcoin has retraced by 32.9% to fall to $125.8.

The weekly trend was bearish, but there is some hope for the bulls that the current retracement could go towards $213-$240, provided the weekly session does not close below $113.4.

Swing traders looking to buy can do so in line with the daily chart, but should remember that the long-term trend was not in their favor.

Why AAVE traders must stay cautious!

The $140 support zone has been breached. The technical indicators on the daily timeframe were firmly bearish. At the same time, the swing structure was just about bullish.

The fair value gap around the 78.6% Fibonacci retracement level (white) at $129 was breached, and the bullish order block around $115 was being tested.

If the market-wide selling continues, it is highly likely Aave’s price structure would take a bearish shift. As things stand, swing traders can wait for a sign of demand, maybe in the form of heavy demand or a price move back above $120, to consider going long.

Final Summary

  • The Aave response to the Binance heist was to freeze their v3 and v4 markets, which was effective but also put selling pressure on the DeFi token and other related assets.
  • In this environment of fear, going long is risky. Swing traders can wait for a clearer conditions before looking for trading opportunities.

data.title: Why Celestia crypto’s breakdown below $0.47 could trigger more TIA losses
data.description:
Celestia [TIA] plunged 14.03% in 24 hours at press time, as fresh macroeconomic uncertainty triggered heavy selling across the altcoin market, deepening its recent losses.

This steep decline accompanied the Federal Reserve’s hawkish stance and persistent inflation concerns, which weakened demand for riskier altcoins.

Particularly, the Federal Reserve preserved its cautious monetary policy stance on the 28th of October. Additionally, September’s PCE inflation matched expectations at 3.6% annually, validating concerns about extended restrictive interest rates.

Despite the price decline, the token’s trading volume interestingly surged 38.04% to $72.72 million.

This divergence implied an elevated trading activity during the sell-off, even though the volume increase could not solely establish sellers’ dominance.

TIA traders retreat as Open Interest collapses

Celestia’s derivatives market registered a considerable contraction in trader exposure, beyond the spot market decline.

According to CoinGlass, TIA’s Open Interest (OI) dropped 28.60% to $75.86 million, suggesting that traders closed positions as the token’s price continued falling. The shrinking OI alone, however, could not distinguish voluntary position closures from forced liquidations.

Therefore, for Celestia, the depreciation emerged in the midst of a broader retreat in the speculative participation. As the derivatives positions diminished, the market encountered reduced leveraged exposure despite the increased trading activity.

Spot and Futures sellers tighten their grip

The bearish pressure notably extended across Celestia‘s spot and derivatives markets, confirming the weakness evident in its price performance.

As CryptoQuant analytics, TIA’s Spot Taker Cumulative Volume Delta (CVD) highlighted taker-sell dominance, implying aggressive sellers outweighed buyers executing market orders. Additionally, the Futures Taker CVD also showed taker-sell dominance, revealing similar behavior among the derivatives investors.

These readings together pointed towards a coordinated bearish pressure across the two markets. Noteworthy, unlike the falling OI, which implied declining outstanding positions, the CVD indicator highlighted the direction of aggressive trading.

The persistent selling across both markets therefore complicated TIA’s recovery attempts, and without a stronger buying participation, the token could struggle to reverse its recent losses.

TIA loses crucial support as bears advance

On the daily timeframe chart, Celestia’s price structure strengthened the bearish outlook after the token broke below the $0.4727 support level.

Notably, the price breakdown emerged after an earlier rejection around the $0.5548 zone, which had already weakened the token’s recovery structure.

The Parabolic SAR indicator, meanwhile, remained above the price at around $0.6616 as of press time, preserving its bearish signal.

Additionally, further weakness emerged from the RSI indicator, which fell to 39.44, remaining below its moving average, and suggesting deteriorating buying strength.

Consequently, the breakdown exposed the $0.3277 level as the next major support, even though buyers still had a better chance of intervening before that level.

A decisive reclaim of the $0.4727 resistance, however, could ease immediate selling pressure and reopen a recovery attempt toward the $0.5548 region.

Final Summary

  • Celestia plunged 14% as selling intensified and traders reduced their derivatives exposure.
  • TIA’s breakdown below $0.4727 raised the risk of further losses toward $0.3277.

data.title: ‘Our collateral resides off-exchange’ – Ethena downplays $8.8M Binance exposure
data.description:
Ethena, the protocol behind the synthetic, yield-generating stablecoin USDe, has downplayed exposure to the Binance hack. The team clarified that all their USDe backing resides offchain with its custodians, not on centralized exchanges. 

In fact, for the Binance scenario, the team claimed only $8.8 million in unrealized PnL (profit and loss) exposure to the platform. 

The total unrealized PNL exposure to Binance is ~$8.8M, far below the excess reserve fund of >$60m.

In a separate update following the FUD tied to the Binance exploit, Ethena added that independent attestors, Chainlink and Llama Risk, have verified its overcollateralized backing for USDe. 

Each of these independent 3rd parties mentioned above have confirmed USDe remains overcollateralised by more than $60m at >101.0%.

But before evaluating the claims, AMBCrypto explored why the community seemed worried about Ethena’s outsized exposure to the exploit. 

Ethena’s massive partnership with Binance

Ethena and Binance recently signed a partnership agreement for RWA (real-world assets) basis trade. This involves Binance’s bStocks, which promised an 11% yield and a great expansion into a $150T opportunity in the equity sector for USDe backing. 

The deal was signed last month, but the exposure seems relatively small. 

According to Ethena, RWA basis accounts for $51 million, or 1.2% of its $4.54 billion collateral for USDe. Beyond the RWA basis, Ethena also uses the crypto basis across Bitcoin [BTC] and Ethereum [ETH] to hunt for yield. The crypto basis segment accounts for about 17% of the USDe backing ($628 million) and is spread across Binance, Deribit, Coinbase, Huobi, Bybit, OKX, and Hyperliquid. 

Collectively, this is about 18% USDe collateral exposure to crypto platforms for RWA and crypto basis. In fact, the largest share of the collateral is DeFi lending ($1.3 billion) across Aave and Morpho. But Aave was also affected and paused operations after the Binance hack. So, the contagion risk fears over Ethena’s exposure to the exploit were warranted. 

However, as the project mentioned, it has off-exchange settlements (OES) or custody arrangements with Coinbase, Copper, and Ceffu. So, the risk may be limited, as the project said. 

In fact, Mikhail Kedzel, Founder of Yumi Finance, confirmed that Binance offers such off-chain arrangements to top institutional players. 

For everyone asking why: it’s because Ethena doesn’t keep funds in Binance’s hot wallet. They keep it with their custodian, and Binance just ‘recognizes’ it as funds stored at the CEX. Stuff only really available to the big guys.

It’s like the ‘custodied collateral lending’ design being explored by Aave. 

That said, the Binance attacker stole and dumped 217 million ENA ($34 million) for ETH. This dragged ENA below $0.19 after a 16% drop. Whether Ethena’s clarification on the Binance hack is enough to stop the pullback remains unclear. 

Final Summary

  • Ethena clarified that it can cover the $8.8 million Binance exposure.
  • Binance attacker sold $33 million in ENA for ETH to avoid seizure and freezing.
